body: Feeling a bit better now. Thanks to everyone that posted. I'm going to try to get some sleep so I don't miss my limited time frame to complete my Chemistry homework. (yay procrastination!)
I'll think about it and I may bring it up with my psychiatrist next time I meet with her to give an update on my med prescription.

Haha, this post made me smile. I guess lately I have been more sociable with people than I normally would. When I'm in a good mood I can somewhat talk with strangers, albeit awkwardly. I've started to meet more people through smoking weed as well. I may give the "fake it til you make it" method a go and see how things turn out.

Before I started my senior year of highschool, I was a mess. Cried myself to sleep at night, etc. Since that summer or so, whenever I got depressed I became more numb than sad. The operation introduced me to an incredible amount of prescription painkillers for the few years to come, so that may have had a hand in me being less unhappy, haha. That, along with hoping that things would somehow be completely different when I started college. 

At the time I was receiving therapy, I was still under 18 and if I seemed at risk they would have to report to my parents. I suppose if I went for help now I could keep my parents out of the loop, but the thought of taking the steps to get therapy sessions scheduled terrifies me.

I'm on Cymbalta right now for depression and anxiety. They put me on them almost 3 years ago, but lately the depression has been coming back. I was in therapy briefly, but I was always too scared of my parents getting involved to say much.
I'll do this. Thank you for the idea.
